title: Remote payload stale despite newer version
description: Investigate whether apply_update_result can download a payload whose internal VERSION is older than remote_version and still apply it as success
hypothesis: Remote windows-VERSION can be newer while windows-app-base.zip content/version is stale due release asset cache or mismatch; launcher does not validate payload VERSION before invoking updater
result_json: {"id":"H1","result_status":"confirmed","findings":"Confirmed: Windows apply_update_result treats a newer windows-VERSION as authoritative, downloads windows-app-base.zip, invokes the updater with remote_version as --release-name, and returns updated=True solely on updater exit code 0. Neither launcher nor updater validates the downloaded payload zip's internal VERSION against remote_version before reporting success.","evidence_for":"packaging/windows/launcher/launcher_main.py:94-116 computes has_update by compare_versions(remote,current) using only the remote version text; lines 82-91 download payload bytes without zip/VERSION inspection; lines 220-235 download the configured payload and pass check['remote_version'] as --release-name; lines 238-241 return ok/updated true when subprocess returncode is 0. packaging/windows/updater/updater_main.py:39-46 extracts the payload into runtime/<release-name> and writes current.txt to args.release_name without reading payload VERSION; lines 47-52 do in-place replacement similarly without VERSION validation. packaging/windows/launcher/runtime_manager.py:177-192 extracts bootstrap payload and writes current.txt to release_name; line 184 only skips an existing runtime if existing VERSION is newer than payload VERSION, not rejecting stale payload. tests/test_windows_launcher_update.py:111-135 mocks payload as raw b'payload-bytes' and still expects updated true and --release-name 2026.05.25.3, proving apply_update_result has no payload VERSION validation. tests/test_runtime_manager.py:210-228 explicitly allows a VERSION downgrade during in-place payload copy, showing stale/lower internal VERSION is not universally treated as failure.","evidence_against":"publish_release builds root windows-VERSION and windows-app-base.zip in the same local publish operation (packaging/windows/publish_release.py:35-55), which reduces intended mismatch risk for correctly published assets, but it does not protect the launcher from a stale cached/mismatched remote payload at update time. No evidence found of a pre-updater payload VERSION check in the Windows launcher path.","error":""}

title: Updater in-place replace does not overwrite files
description: Investigate whether replace_in_place_payload or updater_main can return success without actually overwriting VERSION/main.py in writable install directory
hypothesis: In-place updater extraction or copy logic is flawed and silently leaves old files
result_json: {"id":"H2","result_status":"refuted","findings":"Refuted for the assigned in-place extraction/copy hypothesis: standard payload construction includes VERSION and main.py, replace_in_place_payload overwrites extracted top-level entries by deleting existing destinations before copy, and updater_main returns 0 only after that function completes. I found a related verification gap: launcher apply_update_result reports updated=True solely from updater returncode 0 and tests mock that returncode without verifying files, but that is not evidence that replace_in_place_payload itself silently leaves old VERSION/main.py in normal writable installs.","evidence_for":"Related false-success gap: packaging/windows/launcher/launcher_main.py:226-241 runs the updater and returns {'ok': True, 'updated': True} after returncode 0 without rereading VERSION/main.py or comparing payload fingerprint/content. tests/test_windows_launcher_update.py:122-129 mocks subprocess.run.returncode=0 and asserts updated=True without checking install files. tests/test_runtime_manager.py:142-162 covers replace_in_place_payload but only asserts main.py/static exist, not that existing VERSION/main.py content was overwritten.","evidence_against":"packaging/windows/payload/build_payload.py:14-21 includes main.py and VERSION in the Windows payload and lines 29-30 fail if any included source is missing. packaging/windows/updater/updater_main.py:47-54 uses in-place mode for writable install dirs, calls replace_in_place_payload, writes .payload-ready, then returns 0; exceptions would propagate because they are not caught. packaging/windows/launcher/runtime_manager.py:319-335 extracts payload to a temp dir, then for each top-level extracted entry removes an existing destination with rmtree/unlink before copytree/copy2, so included VERSION/main.py are overwritten rather than skipped. packaging/windows/launcher/runtime_manager.py:274-287 also repairs bootstrap payload installs by extractall and writes marker only after extraction; payload_matches_install at 300-316 byte-compares manifest entries before skipping.","error":""}

title: Post-update verification missing
description: Investigate whether launcher reports ok updated true without re-reading installed version after updater exits
hypothesis: apply_update_result trusts updater returncode and clears pending_update without verifying current_payload_version >= remote_version
result_json: {"id":"H3","result_status":"confirmed","findings":"Confirmed for both Windows and macOS launchers: apply_update_result treats subprocess returncode 0 as success, clears pending_update, and returns ok/updated true without re-reading current_payload_version or checking it against remote_version after the updater exits. Existing tests also assert success with a mocked returncode 0 but do not simulate unchanged installed version.","evidence_for":"Windows: packaging/windows/launcher/launcher_main.py:209 calls check_for_updates before running updater; lines 226-239 run updater and only fail on nonzero returncode; line 240 clears pending_update; line 241 returns {'ok': True, 'updated': True, ...check} using the pre-update check. macOS mirrors this: packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:265 calls check_for_updates before updater; lines 282-297 only gate on returncode; line 298 clears pending_update; line 299 returns ok/updated true. The available version reader exists at packaging/windows/launcher/runtime_manager.py:87 and packaging/macos/launcher/runtime_manager.py:76, and pending_update_from_state uses it before update at packaging/windows/launcher/launcher_main.py:126-127 and packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:211-212, but apply_update_result does not call it after subprocess.run. Tests reinforce the gap: tests/test_windows_launcher_update.py:122-129 and tests/test_macos_launcher_update.py:182-189 set run.return_value.returncode = 0 and assert result['updated'] without changing/re-reading installed version.","evidence_against":"No counterexample found. apply_update_result does re-check remote/current before launching and clears stale pending state when has_update is false, but there is no post-updater verification path in the inspected Windows/macOS launcher code. Tests for auto-update on next launch mock apply_update_result directly at tests/test_windows_launcher_update.py:203-204 and tests/test_macos_launcher_update.py:264-265, so they do not validate installed payload version either.","error":""}
